records.description: A normal retail offer from an ordinary provider (e.g. Serper-sourced) carries no commerceType field at all — absence is the realistic representation of retail, not an explicit 'retail' string.
records.notes: supabase/functions/scan-identify/shoppingProvider.ts:32-37 — RecommendedProduct.commerceType is optional and only ever set by the Poshmark provider; every other provider (Serper, Brave, Farfetch, KicksCrew) leaves it unset. An ordinary retail offer is represented by the field's absence, not by an explicit commerceType: 'retail' string, since no real source ever writes that literal.

records.description: A Poshmark resale listing explicitly carries commerceType: 'resale', the only provider in the real system that ever sets this field.
records.notes: supabase/functions/scan-identify/poshmarkProvider.ts:213,219 — the Poshmark normalizer sets type: 'retail' (it is a real purchasable listing) and commerceType: 'resale' (its provenance) as two independent fields.

records.description: A retail offer and a Poshmark resale offer for the same garment are shown side by side, with neither ranked above the other on the basis of commerceType.
records.notes: supabase/functions/scan-identify/shoppingProvider.ts:32-37 — commerceType 'must never carry a ranking bonus or penalty (retailer-neutrality is a hard rule)'; a retail and a resale offer for the same garment must be presented without either being preferred on that basis alone.

records.description: An offer from a generic/ambiguous provider has no commerceType field and no other signal that would let it be attributed to either retail or resale — it must not be defaulted to retail.
records.notes: SYNTHETIC boundary probe: constructed to exercise the case where commerceType is absent AND the offer cannot be inferred as retail from other fields (type: 'similar', a generic non-registered source). Grounded in shoppingProvider.ts:32-37's optionality, but the specific 'ambiguous provider' framing was not observed in real code and is deliberately invented to test that absence is never silently coerced into 'retail'.

records.description: A resale offer carries condition-like information inside the generic free-text availability field, since no dedicated structured condition enum exists in the real source.
records.notes: poshmarkProvider.ts:213-219 shows only generic size/availability/variant fields on any offer, retail or resale — no dedicated condition field exists in RecommendedProduct (shoppingProvider.ts:15-45). The availability field here is reused as free text to carry condition information; it is not a structured condition enum.

records.description: A resale offer whose availability signal indicates the listing is gone normalizes to an Out of Stock label rather than being silently dropped.
records.notes: components/scan-results/types.ts:213-221 (availabilityLabel()) normalizes 'sold_out' to 'Out of Stock'; the offer itself is still surfaced (not removed from the list), only its availability state changes.
